comments.body:
🚨 **BLOCKING: CI red — crap ratchet fails (15 new functions over threshold 8), worst offender is dead code**

The `crap` check failed on head `056b9cea` (`ci_failures.md`, log line `0 regression(s), 15 new over threshold, 8 improvement(s)... exit code 2`), so the merge gate is red. The single worst offender is this function:

```
sameBuildAndEnv    js/common/tcTriage.js    CC 8    Cov 0.0%    CRAP 72.0
```

`sameBuildAndEnv` is **never called anywhere** — not by `triageValidatedGuard` (which uses `sameBuild` + `envChanged` directly), not by any caller, not by any test (`grep -rn sameBuildAndEnv` finds only its definition and export). Deleting it removes the 72-CRAP entry entirely.

The remaining 14 over-threshold functions need decomposition before the ratchet passes (new functions must land ≤ 8):

- `js/postStoryTestAutomationResults.js`: `triageBugFailures` (19.5), `entryRoleMeta` (17.1), `handleBugWithProductFailure` (16.1), `currentBuildSha` (10.4)
- `js/common/tcMaintenanceLedger.js`: `normalizeFinding` (17), `findingFromVerdict` (16), `findingFromDevClaim` (11), `findingLine` (11.2)
- `js/common/tcRunRegistry.js`: `recordGreen` (16), `recordFailure` (14)
- `js/common/tcTriage.js`: `pickEvidence` (14), `resolveTcRole` (10)
- `js/developBugAndCreatePR.js`: `completeTestSuspectedPath` (12.2)
- `js/unit-tests/test_postStoryTestAutomationResults.js`: `triageModule` (9)

Concrete refactor guidance: extract per-entry step helpers (`triageBugFailures` → one-entry function), table-drive `pickEvidence`/`normalizeFinding` field copying with a `[key, sourceKeys]` loop, split `recordGreen`/`recordFailure` entry construction into a shared `mergeEntryState` helper, and split `entryRoleMeta` source selection into a small resolver chain. All are pure functions — the existing 51 new unit tests keep passing through mechanical extraction.

comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: dead code — `bits` is built and never used**

In `findingLine` (tcMaintenanceLedger.js:349-352) the `bits` array is populated with three conditional pushes and then discarded — the `return` statement below builds its own string from `f.tcKey`/`f.errorClass`/`f.testPath`/`f.occurrences` directly. The `bits` block is dead code that inflates complexity (the CRAP report flags `findingLine` at 11.2) and misleads readers into thinking it formats the output.

Delete the `bits` block (or, if the multi-part line was intended, actually render from `bits.join(' — ')` — but then the `dev claim`/`claimedVerdict` suffixes must move into it too, since today a dev finding renders its testPath twice-shaped: once via `bits` (dropped) and once via the return string).

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the bounce comment lists every TC twice**

`bugReturnComment` builds its own list under the header "The following Test Cases failed with a product regression:" (postStoryTestAutomationResults.js:744-745) and then appends `tcTriage.buildBounceComment(bouncedVerdicts)` — which opens with the **identical header and repeats the same TC list** (tcTriage.js:303-306). The posted comment therefore contains the same header + list twice back-to-back, only differing in the evidence suffix.

Render one list: either keep the legacy `failureList` and pass the verdicts only for the attribution paragraph, or drop the local list and let `buildBounceComment` (which already carries `failureSummary` per TC) own the section. A regression test asserting the TC key appears exactly once in the comment would pin this.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: in a mixed bounce+route run, routed findings are never staged or digested**

When `triage.bounced.length > 0` the function returns immediately after finalizing the bounced TCs — the `stageRoutedBugTestCases(triage.routed, ...)` call and the triage-digest `postComment` below it never run. A run that produces one earned bounce *and* (say) an environment-shifted guard leaves the routed TC at its previous status and its finding visible only inside the machine marker — no human-visible digest, inconsistent with the non-bounce path where the same verdict stages the TC and posts the digest. `escalated` verdicts are likewise reported in the result payload but never staged on either path.

Fix: before the bounce branch, stage routed TCs and append the triage/escalation digest sections to the bounce comment (or post the digest regardless of route), so every attributed finding gets the same human surface on every route.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: same-build red with missing env fingerprints is auto-classified "flaky" — contradicts the module's own evidence doctrine**

`triageValidatedGuard` treats a same-SHA red as `'flaky-same-build'` whenever `envChanged()` is false — including the case where **neither side has an env fingerprint** (the agent omitted `envFingerprint`, cf. the instruction "when you can identify the environment... record it"). Yet this module's own docstring for `sameBuildAndEnv` states: *"A missing half on either side never proves sameness — the comparison is evidence, not a default."* The live triage path does exactly what the doctrine forbids, defaulting an unproven case to "flaky" and routing it to maintenance.

Please confirm the intended reading. Options: route missing-fingerprint same-build reds to the `'rerun-requested-on-last-green-build'`/unknown-env reason instead of asserting `flaky-same-build`, or require both fingerprints before the flaky/environment-shift classification (falling through to the differential request otherwise). If "flaky by default" is deliberate, document it at the branch so the doctrine comment stops contradicting the code.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: legacy bounce path is now gated on agent-supplied `acVerdict` — confirm the degradation is intended**

`triageAcGated` bounces a validated own-oracle TC **only** when `acVerdict === 'violated'`; without an AC verdict it routes to `'own-oracle-ac-recheck'` (rework), and the run returns `status: 'test_maintenance'` with the bug untouched. Previously any red linked TC bounced the bug. So a bug run whose result entries lack the new metadata — an agent run that ignores the updated prompt contract, a hand-crafted or older-format `story_test_automation_result.json`, or a consuming repo that pins this submodule without updating its automation agent — will never bounce: every red degrades to rework/maintenance and the bug stalls in In Testing (the only exit being the redRounds escalation, which itself only fires via the `redRounds` registry streak).

The PR description claims "bounded legacy bounce path preserved" — in shape yes, but only when the agent actually emits `acVerdict`. Please confirm this fail-safe degradation is the accepted default for non-compliant results, and consider a tracker-comment hint when a failed own-oracle entry carries **none** of the new fields (`acVerdict`, `retryStatus`, `errorClass` all absent), so a stalled bug is diagnosable as "agent didn't follow the schema" rather than "product didn't regress".

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the bounce gate trusts the agent-copied `role`/`verifies` over the linked TC's own metadata**

`entryRoleMeta` returns the **result entry first**: if the automation agent supplied `role`/`verifies` (which the updated schema now instructs it to do on every failed entry), the linked TC's own metadata (`linkedEntry`, `linkedEntry.fields`) is never consulted. The entire scoping decision of gh-1329 — own oracle vs sibling vs guard, i.e. whether a TC may ever bounce the bug — thus rests on an LM-copied string. A hallucinated `verifies: "BUG-2"` silently demotes the bug's own acceptance oracle to `ROLE_SIBLING`, which by design can never bounce — the failure mode is invisible (no warning, verdict looks perfectly ordinary).

Since the TC description stamping is mechanical-truth-in-progress (declared guidance-only in the PR concerns), consider at least: (a) preferring `linkedEntry`/`fields` metadata when present (the TC ticket is the durable record; the result file is per-run), and (b) logging a warning when the entry's `verifies` disagrees with a linked-TC-provided value, so a mis-scoped oracle leaves a trace instead of silently demoting the gate.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: silent catches + duplicated bookkeeping plumbing in `completeTestSuspectedPath`**

Two issues in one place:

1. `try { tracker.postComment(ticketKey, ...); } catch (e) {}` (twice, developBugAndCreatePR.js:668-672) swallows failures with no log. The sibling implementation in this same PR (`postMarkerIfChanged`) logs `console.warn('Failed to post', label, 'marker (non-fatal):', e)` — a silently-dropped ledger marker means the next run rebuilds from the stale ledger and the finding's `occurrences` history drifts with nothing in the logs to explain it. Log the warnings.
2. The comment-fetching IIFE and the `machineAuthorOptsOf` construction duplicate `bugTrackedComments`/`machineAuthorOptsOf` in postStoryTestAutomationResults.js (and call `tracker.getIssue(ticketKey)` twice — once for the truthiness check, once for `.fields`). Extract one shared "load bug bookkeeping (comments + author opts)" helper into a common module and call it from both legs.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: `currentBuildSha` shells out once per result entry**

Both call sites in `triageBugFailures` (failed branch line 880, green branch line 918) invoke `currentBuildSha(result, entry, ctx.workingDir)`, which falls through to `runInRepo('git rev-parse HEAD', ...)` whenever the entry/result don't carry a SHA. For a bug with N linked TCs that is up to N identical subprocess invocations per run. Resolve the build SHA once per run (a `var buildSha = currentBuildSha(result, null, ctx.workingDir)` before the `forEach`) and pass it into both branches — the per-entry override (`entry.sha`) can still win inside the helper.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: `note` duplicates `reason` for automation-sourced findings**

`normalizeFinding` sets both `reason: src.reason || null` and `note: truncate(firstDefined(src, ['note', 'reason']))` (tcMaintenanceLedger.js:124). Every automation finding built by `findingFromVerdict` carries `reason` (e.g. `'environment-shift'`), so `note` becomes a truncated copy of `reason` — redundant payload in every marker comment. Only `findingFromDevClaim` produces a genuinely additive `note` (reason + evidence pointer). Consider `note: firstDefined(src, ['note'])` (drop the `reason` fallback) so the two fields stay distinct.
